# Independent shared-common Bidi and table diagnostic review

Reviewed patch `bidi-table-probes-v5.patch`, SHA-256 `6ee1bb1416946cda2a681ede102e7e741ad7c19b5e6b1405e9dc003b7bbc2d27`, against `cd716775d7a61d434413b4b7671b27237ceff38c`. It applies cleanly in an independent worktree. It changes diagnostic tests and two new helpers only; no production source, frozen ledger, historical proof, or shared source checker is changed. Google and 2026 Ryan Lester notices are retained.

The Bidi successor authenticates the frozen 25-use seed and exact `0c25` history using Git without replacement objects or lazy fetch; classifies 23 old stubs removed and two owned uses retained; verifies exact old-to-current import/export changes for 21 family modules, 21 family public exports and root public export; and retains a main-only, source-identification scope. It does not credit the old Bidi admission. The existing old-path branch remains for checkouts retaining the previous root stub; no actual 21.x runtime or full 21.x requalification was run.

Reexecuted the exact v5 public diagnostic independently: 25 uses, 49 source negatives, six original/minimum-peer subject runs totaling 36 cases and 17 runtime mutations; output SHA-256 `19915125ed39bfe54d2de628daafb2a53825c2eaee8abe2fdbeed4db5a0fb3ed`, identical to the author's. Source metadata and real Angular provider/runtime tests here do not establish current native DOM or packed consumer acceptance. The separately retained experimental unpacked-artifact controls start from artifact `38aff30d...` and change exactly the listed FESM/declaration inputs: missing A11y fails the forced-color assertion, wrong export fails identity, and missing Bidi fails Dir. These are recompiled diagnostic mutants, not upstream mutants or a fresh release artifact.

The opt-in table bridge verifies two exact source transitions from `ebe2f14...` through `0c25...` to the new shared module, verifies the old stub is absent and owned core unchanged, then feeds the exact historical bytes to the existing 26-role review. Independent opt-in caller output SHA-256 `8c48cc17ebf3a2595cd5a93b1722a74c98928058974b1fd2a6dedc22a71ee100` reproduces 43 source/evidence corruptions rejected, two late reads rejected, and historical-only 148 finite cases. It explicitly reports canonical_ledger_checked=false, historical runtime cases, and no current packed table rendering qualification. The default table caller remains fail-closed: independent run rejected `preparation changed canonical bytes`. No frozen table ledger acceptance is inferred.

Independent adversarial finding and fix: v2 accepted a checkout differing only in package major 21 while reporting line main in both standalone successors; both outputs were byte-identical to the 22-version positives. V4 added actual package-line/22.1.7 declared-peer checks and repeated line checks during bridged reads; v5 preserves that fix. Reproduced on exact v5: both standalone successors and both outer probes reject the same 21-version-only mutation. Separately confirmed wrong CDK peer floor rejects in both v4 source-identical logic and recorded default ledger failure. This is a fail-closed negative control, not a successful 21.x execution. V5 independently reproduced exact Bidi/table outputs including bridge/producer source hashes. Git-history reads disable replacement objects and lazy fetching.

Remaining limits: upstream Bidi admission still fails closed at its older source context and remains separate; the table successor intentionally does not validate current canonical ledger rows, current native packed rendering, full floors, or G11. The previous generated CommonModule constructor exception and full current artifact/SSR/a11y gates remain separate. Historical records and older checkout behavior must be preserved during composition.

Conclusion: bounded source-transition diagnostics and the opt-in historical table bridge are supported for MAIN after the line fix, with the above explicit limits. No canonical integration, 21.x, security, full runtime or release pass is granted.
